findings: All 13 workflow jobs passed, including the four-lane exact WAV and PCM comparison.

Windows Swift Debug and Release each reported 91 tests, executed 90, skipped one opt-in generator and failed none. Each executed all 14 new PortableCPRReviewTests and all six existing SharedCPRImportTests without skips.

macOS portable Debug and Release each reported 93 tests, executed 92, skipped one opt-in generator and failed none. Each executed all 14 new PortableCPRReviewTests and all seven existing SharedCPRImportTests without skips.
The existing macOS application suite reported 379 tests, executed 262, skipped 117 private-fixture or opt-in generator tests and failed none. Its seven shared importer tests executed without skips.

The new authored review/import controls cover read-only state and history, exact revisions, token lifecycle, explicit partial consent, new destinations, source changes, dirty-save continuity, unknown-only import refusal, historical replay, bounded ordered pages, and post-publication readback failures without replacing the active session.

All four production helpers passed 91 interactive checks and all 16 CPR-import gates, preserving exact authored source/report bytes and rejecting tampering. The fixture review has 15 items on one page; separate Swift controls exercise larger pages and bounds.
All four helpers retained the locked 11-waveform, 17600-bin, 33-tick ruler and exact example/source PCM results.
Unchanged C DSP, native lifecycle and public SoXR gates passed. The hosted audio endpoints were unavailable; no audio playback was measured.
boundaries: The 46 retained CI records are byte-exact downloaded artifacts already sanitized by the workflow; this collection applies no further edits.
source-audition-expected.json is byte-exact repository source from the recorded commit, not generated by the CI run.

Selected text records were scanned for private home/local temporary paths, personal namespace terms, email addresses, credentials and private-key headers; no matches were found. Public GitHub ownership remains visible.

The ruler is shared application display policy. Its optional native clock arithmetic retains its separately bounded static-evidence contract; ruler output does not convert timing or resolve source events.
No proprietary reference application was executed; authored controls do not establish general project compatibility, full Windows parity or reference-runtime fidelity.
Hosted Windows audio endpoints were unavailable. No device playback or audible output was measured.
Windows Release test binaries use optimized compilation with cross-module optimization disabled for test discovery. Inspector and session production builds use normal production flags.
Application packaging, native-window validation and visual fidelity are recorded separately.

This component run establishes shared-core authored controls and production-helper protocol execution. Windows native-window CPR import behavior belongs to the separate application workflow and is not inferred here.
No Windows application ZIP was downloaded or released during this component evidence-retention step.
